prompt: Research one sovereign trusted small-drone supply-chain investment idea.

inputs.seed_claim: Battlefield attrition, civil UAS adoption, and trusted-supplier policies may redirect procurement toward allied drone platforms and critical components, with Ukrainian designs offering industrialisation potential.
inputs.drivers: Military attrition; public-safety and industrial adoption; U.S. and EU trusted-supplier rules; Chinese dependence; Ukrainian innovation; financing, certification, and scale.
inputs.value_chain: Small-UAS manufacturers; motors, batteries, and power electronics; flight controllers, sensors, communications, autonomy software; electronics manufacturing; defence and civil procurement.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed requires funded multi-year U.S./EU procurement, Drone Alliance orders, industrialised Ukrainian designs, and rising allied-component share without cost or performance loss.
inputs.invalidation: Chinese cost and ecosystem advantages persist, allied components remain dependent on China, procurement fragments, BVLOS approvals lag, or commoditisation prevents durable margins.
